method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Perioperative management of RA: holding DMARDs and biologics for surgery
topic.coverageNote: Gives continue-versus-hold rules and two biologic examples. The 2022 ACR/AAHKS update was not an open PMC full text, so newer changes after 2019 are not added.

mcqs.question: Which conventional DMARDs does the summarized perioperative guidance say to continue without interruption?

options.C: Methotrexate is always stopped 8 weeks before surgery
options.D: Leflunomide is the only drug that must be stopped
options.E: All DMARDs are held for one dosing interval

mcqs.explanation: Guidance summarized in the review continues methotrexate, leflunomide, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine throughout the perioperative period.

sourceRefs.excerpt: continuing conventional DMARDs methotrexate, leflunomide, sulfasalazine, and hydroxychloroquine throughout the perioperative period without interruption.

mcqs.question: What evidence does the review cite for not stopping conventional DMARDs?

options.A: Low non-operative infection risk with methotrexate, and small trials in which stopping conventional DMARDs gave a similar or higher postoperative infection risk
options.B: A 4000-patient trial proving biologics are safe to continue
options.C: Infection risk rises if methotrexate is continued
options.D: Hydroxychloroquine must be washed out for 6 months

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Low non-operative infection risk with methotrexate, and small trials in which stopping conventional DMARDs gave a similar or higher postoperative infection risk
mcqs.explanation: Infection risk with methotrexate outside surgery was low, and small randomized trials showed similar or increased postoperative infection when conventional DMARDs were stopped.

sourceRefs.excerpt: and data from small randomized trials showing similar or increased risk of post-operative infections with discontinuation of conventional DMARDs before surgery

mcqs.question: How long before surgery are biologics held?

options.A: One dosing interval, not a half-life-based interval
options.C: They are continued on the morning of surgery

mcqs.correctAnswerText: One dosing interval, not a half-life-based interval
mcqs.explanation: Biologics are held for one dosing interval. The dosing interval was chosen rather than half-life because half-life was felt not to correlate as well with duration of action.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the panel recommended holding biologics for one dosing interval prior to surgery. The dosing interval was used rather than half-life because the half-life was not felt to correlate as well with the duration of action.

mcqs.question: A patient receives infliximab every 8 weeks. When is the last dose before surgery under this guidance?
mcqs.explanation: Infliximab every 8 weeks means the last dose is 9 weeks before surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: a patient receiving infliximab every 8 weeks would last receive the medication 9 weeks before surgery

mcqs.question: A patient receives adalimumab every 2 weeks. When is the last preoperative dose?

options.D: Adalimumab is continued without a gap

mcqs.explanation: Adalimumab every two weeks means the last dose is 3 weeks before surgery.

sourceRefs.excerpt: a patient receiving adalimumab every two weeks would receive the medication 3 weeks
